title: The vision begins
summary: The angel tells Nephi to look. Nephi sees many nations and kingdoms, and the angel identifies them as the nations and kingdoms of the Gentiles.
characters: The angel who appeared to Nephi

explicit_facts.text: The angel tells Nephi to look, and Nephi sees many nations and kingdoms.
The angel asks what Nephi sees; Nephi replies that he sees many nations and kingdoms.
The angel identifies them as the nations and kingdoms of the Gentiles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi and the angel are together as Nephi looks upon a vision of nations and kingdoms.
unspecified_visual_details: The angel's appearance, the setting, and how the nations and kingdoms are visually represented.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel who appeared to Nephi
The angel who appeared to Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: I behold many nations and kingdoms.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Nephi

spoken_dialogue.text: These are the nations and kingdoms of the Gentiles.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel who appeared to Nephi

prohibited_inventions: Do not assign particular identities or names to the nations or kingdoms.

title: The great church
summary: Nephi sees the formation of a great church among the Gentile nations. The angel describes it, and Nephi sees the devil as its founder.
characters: The angel who appeared to Nephi

explicit_facts.text: Nephi sees the formation of a great church among the nations of the Gentiles.
The angel describes the church as slaying, torturing, binding, and bringing saints of God into captivity.
Nephi sees the great and abominable church and sees the devil as its founder.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The vision may represent the church's formation and the angel's description through symbolic imagery.
unspecified_visual_details: The church's appearance, the devil's appearance, and any specific acts of violence or captivity shown.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold the formation of a church which is most abominable above all other churches,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel who appeared to Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The church's described acts and its founder are part of Nephi's vision.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify this church with any named historical institution.
Do not depict unreported specific acts, victims, or details of torture.

title: Desires of the church
summary: Nephi sees precious goods and many harlots. The angel identifies them as the desires of the great and abominable church; Nephi also sees the church destroy saints for the praise of the world and bring them into captivity.
characters: The angel who appeared to Nephi

explicit_facts.text: Nephi sees gold, silver, silks, scarlets, fine-twined linen, precious clothing, and many harlots.
The angel says these things are the desires of the great and abominable church.
For the praise of the world, the church destroys saints of God and brings them into captivity.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The goods and harlots may be shown as elements of Nephi's vision.
unspecified_visual_details: The people, designs, or surroundings associated with the goods and the church's actions.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold the gold, and the silver, and the silks, and the scarlets, and the fine-twined linen, and the precious clothing, and the harlots, are the desires of this great and abominable church.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel who appeared to Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The goods and harlots are identified as desires, not as a literal supernatural manifestation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add identities, biographies, or specific actions for the harlots or saints.
Do not depict specific destruction or captivity details beyond what the text states.

title: Waters divide the peoples
summary: Nephi sees many waters dividing the Gentiles from the seed of his brethren. The angel says God's wrath is upon the seed of Nephi's brethren.
characters: The angel who appeared to Nephi

explicit_facts.text: Nephi sees many waters dividing the Gentiles from the seed of his brethren.
The angel says the wrath of God is upon the seed of Nephi's brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The vision can show waters between two groups without specifying their identities individually.
unspecified_visual_details: The waters' geography, the location of either group, and any visible manifestation of God's wrath.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold the wrath of God is upon the seed of thy brethren.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel who appeared to Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The statement about wrath is the angel's interpretation; the verse does not describe a visible form of divine wrath.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show destruction or a physical manifestation of wrath not narrated in the verses.

title: A man crosses the waters
summary: Nephi beholds a man among the Gentiles, separated by many waters from the seed of Nephi's brethren. The Spirit of God comes down and works upon the man. The man goes across the waters to the seed of Nephi's brethren in the promised land.
characters: an unnamed man among the Gentiles

explicit_facts.text: Nephi beholds a man among the Gentiles, separated from the seed of his brethren by many waters.
The Spirit of God comes down and works upon the man.
The man goes across the many waters to the seed of Nephi's brethren in the promised land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Water separates the man from the seed of Nephi's brethren.
The man's departure and arrival can be shown in sequence, rather than as one moment.
unspecified_visual_details: The man's identity and appearance.
His means of travel and route.
The Spirit of God's visual form.

narration.text: And I looked and beheld a man among the Gentiles,
and I beheld the Spirit of God, that it came down and wrought upon the man;
and he went forth upon the many waters, even unto the seed of my brethren, who were in the promised land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The first-person narrator is Nephi. The source does not say what the Spirit of God looked like; the narration must not add “Nephi” inside a verse quotation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name the man or specify a vessel or route.
Do not invent a visible form for the Spirit of God.
Do not add an angel or dialogue.

title: Other Gentiles leave captivity
summary: The narrator beholds the Spirit of God working upon other Gentiles, who go forth out of captivity upon the many waters.

explicit_facts.text: The narrator beholds the Spirit of God.
The Spirit of God works upon other Gentiles, who go forth out of captivity upon the many waters.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Gentiles may be shown traveling upon water.
unspecified_visual_details: The Gentiles’ number and identities, their means of travel, and the location of their captivity are not specified.
The Spirit of God’s appearance is not described.

narration.text: And it came to pass that I beheld the Spirit of God, that it wrought upon other Gentiles; and they went forth out of captivity, upon the many waters.

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the Gentiles or invent details of their captivity or voyage.
Do not invent a visible form for the Spirit of God.

title: Peoples on the land of promise
summary: Nephi beholds many multitudes of Gentiles on the land of promise. The seed of his brethren are scattered before them and smitten. He beholds the Spirit of the Lord upon the Gentiles, who prosper and obtain the land for their inheritance.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi beholds many multitudes of Gentiles on the land of promise, and the seed of his brethren are scattered before them and smitten.
Nephi beholds the wrath of God upon the seed of his brethren.
Nephi beholds the Spirit of the Lord upon the Gentiles, who prosper and obtain the land for their inheritance.
Nephi describes the Gentiles as white, exceedingly fair and beautiful, like his people before they were slain.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The scattering and smiting can be shown as non-graphic physical action.
unspecified_visual_details: Clothing, terrain, the individuals' identities, and the specific acts by which the Gentiles obtain the land.

narration.text: and they were scattered before the Gentiles and were smitten.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses do not describe a visible form for the wrath of God or the Spirit of the Lord.
The comparison to Nephi's people before they were slain does not place those people in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible form for the Spirit of the Lord or the wrath of God.
Do not depict gore or invent additional physical traits, named individuals, or specific acts of land acquisition.

title: The Gentiles humble themselves
summary: Nephi beholds the Gentiles who went out of captivity humble themselves before the Lord. Their mother Gentiles gather on water and land to battle against them. The power of God is with the former group, and God's wrath is upon those gathered against them.
characters: the Gentiles who went out of captivity

explicit_facts.text: Nephi beholds the Gentiles who went out of captivity humble themselves before the Lord; the Lord's power is with them.
Their mother Gentiles gather upon the waters and the land to battle against them.
The power of God is with the Gentiles who went out of captivity, and God's wrath is upon those gathered against them to battle.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The groups can be shown separately to make clear who is gathering against whom.
unspecified_visual_details: The groups' appearances and the specific land and waters are not described.
No visible appearance of the Lord or of divine power or wrath is described.

narration.text: And I beheld that their mother Gentiles were gathered together upon the waters, and upon the land also, to battle against them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses describe a gathering to battle, not a battle taking place.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle, victory, or visible divine intervention.
Do not give the Lord an invented visible appearance.

title: Delivered from other nations
summary: Nephi beholds that the Gentiles who went out of captivity were delivered by the power of God from the hands of all other nations.
characters: the Gentiles who went out of captivity

explicit_facts.text: Nephi beheld the Gentiles who had gone out of captivity.
The Gentiles were delivered by the power of God out of the hands of all other nations.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Gentiles may be portrayed as no longer under the control of other nations.
unspecified_visual_details: The place and visible manner of the deliverance.

narration.text: And I, Nephi, beheld that the Gentiles that had gone out of captivity were delivered by the power of God out of the hands of all other nations.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not describe the means of deliverance or God's visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific battle, rescue, miracle, or visible appearance of God.

title: A book is carried among them
summary: Nephi sees people prosper in the land and a book carried among them. An angel asks whether he knows the book's meaning, and Nephi says he does not.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi beholds people prospering in the land.
Nephi beholds a book carried among them.
The angel asks Nephi whether he knows the meaning of the book.
Nephi says he does not know.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A book is visible among the unnamed people.
unspecified_visual_details: The people's identities and the manner of their prosperity.
The book's appearance and who carries it.
Where Nephi and the angel are as they speak.

spoken_dialogue.text: Knowest thou the meaning of the book?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: the angel

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the unnamed people or specify what the book contains.
Do not add text, markings, or identifying features to the book.

title: The record of the Jews
summary: Nephi beholds the book. The angel tells him that it is a record of the Jews containing the Lord’s covenants and many prophecies, and says these things go forth from the Jews to the Gentiles in purity.

explicit_facts.text: Nephi beholds the book.
The angel describes the book as a record of the Jews containing the Lord’s covenants with the house of Israel and many prophecies of holy prophets.
The angel compares the record to the engravings on the plates of brass, says it contains fewer, and calls it of great worth to the Gentiles.
The angel says the book contained the fulness of the gospel of the Lord when it proceeded from the mouth of a Jew, and that the twelve apostles bear record of the Lord.
The angel says these things go forth from the Jews in purity to the Gentiles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The book Nephi beholds may be visible while the angel speaks to him.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the book’s physical appearance, and the angel’s appearance are not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold it proceedeth out of the mouth of a Jew.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel of the Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: Wherefore, these things go forth from the Jews in purity unto the Gentiles, according to the truth which is in God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel of the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The book’s proceeding from the mouth of a Jew describes its source, not a visible event in which a book emerges from a mouth.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a book emerging from a mouth.
Do not place the unnamed Jew, the twelve apostles, or the holy prophets physically in this scene.
Do not invent an appearance for the angel.

title: Plain and precious things removed
summary: The angel says that after the book goes from the Jews to the Gentiles through the twelve apostles, the great and abominable church takes away plain and precious parts of the gospel and covenants to pervert the Lord's ways, blind eyes, and harden hearts. Nephi sees many such things removed from the book.
characters: The angel who appeared to Nephi

explicit_facts.text: After the book goes forth through the twelve apostles from the Jews to the Gentiles, the angel says the great and abominable church takes away plain and precious parts of the gospel and covenants.
The angel says this is done to pervert the Lord's ways, blind eyes, and harden hearts.
Nephi sees many plain and precious things taken away from the book of the Lamb of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The removal may be represented symbolically, without inventing specific text or historical actors.
unspecified_visual_details: Who specifically removes the material, when it occurs, and what the removed content looks like.

spoken_dialogue.text: they have taken away from the gospel of the Lamb many parts which are plain and most precious;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel who appeared to Nephi

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The removal and its stated purposes are the angel's explanation within Nephi's vision.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent missing passages, specific editors, or a literal visible process of changing the book.

title: The book goes forth among the Gentiles
summary: After plain and precious things are taken away, the book goes forth among all the nations of the Gentiles, including across many waters. Because of what was taken away, exceedingly many stumble, and Satan has great power over them.

explicit_facts.text: Plain and precious things were taken out of the book.
After these things were taken away, the book goes forth to all the nations of the Gentiles, including across many waters.
Because of the things taken away, exceedingly many stumble, and Satan has great power over them.

unspecified_visual_details: The book’s appearance
The identities and appearances of the Gentiles
The geography across the many waters

narration.text: it goeth forth unto all the nations of the Gentiles
an exceedingly great many do stumble, yea, insomuch that Satan hath great power over them.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Stumbling expresses the consequence described in the verse; it does not require a literal falling scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Satan’s appearance or invent acts of deception.
Do not turn stumbling into an invented physical incident.
Do not invent a vessel, route, or specific nation.

title: The Gentiles Will Not Destroy the Seed
summary: The Gentiles have gone forth out of captivity and been lifted up by God's power on the choice land. The Lord will not suffer them to utterly destroy the mixture of the addressee's seed among his brethren or to destroy his brethren's seed. Nor will he suffer the Gentiles to remain forever in blindness caused by precious parts of the gospel being kept back.
characters: the mixture of the addressee's seed among his brethren
the seed of the addressee's brethren
locations: the choice land covenanted to the addressee's father for his seed's inheritance

explicit_facts.text: The Gentiles have gone forth out of captivity and been lifted up by the power of God above other nations.
The choice land was covenanted to the addressee's father for his seed's inheritance.
The Lord God will not suffer the Gentiles to utterly destroy the mixture of the addressee's seed among his brethren.
The Lord God will not suffer the Gentiles to destroy the seed of the addressee's brethren.
The Lord God will not suffer the Gentiles to remain forever in blindness caused by plain and precious parts of the gospel of the Lamb being kept back by the abominable church.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The Gentiles and the land may be represented as things the addressee beholds, without staging the future destruction that the verses say will not occur.
unspecified_visual_details: The land's terrain and the people's appearance are not described.

narration.text: the Gentiles who have gone forth out of captivity
Neither will he suffer that the Gentiles shall destroy the seed of thy brethren.
Neither will the Lord God suffer that the Gentiles shall forever remain in that awful state of blindness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Blindness is part of the teaching, not a narrated physical condition.
The verses do not identify the speaker; the quoted text is therefore assigned to narration rather than a named character.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a battle, destruction, physical blindness, or a visible act of divine protection.
Do not invent the speaker's identity or depict the Lord God or the Lamb as visibly appearing.

title: Mercy to the Gentiles
summary: The Lamb says he will be merciful to the Gentiles while visiting the remnant of the house of Israel in great judgment. The angel relays the Lamb's further words about visiting and smiting the remnant, the Gentiles stumbling, and the Lamb bringing much of his gospel to the Gentiles in his own power.
characters: The angel who appeared to Nephi
the remnant of the house of Israel

explicit_facts.text: The Lamb says he will be merciful to the Gentiles while visiting the remnant of the house of Israel in great judgment.
The angel says the Lamb will visit the remnant, the seed of Nephi's father, in judgment and smite them by the hand of the Gentiles.
The angel says the Gentiles will stumble because plain and precious parts of the gospel were kept back.
The Lamb says he will be merciful to the Gentiles and bring much of his gospel to them in his own power.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The teaching can be conveyed as off-screen speech over a conservative vision setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lamb's appearance and any visible form of judgment, stumbling, or mercy.

spoken_dialogue.text: I will be merciful unto the Gentiles,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lamb of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lamb's words are reported within the angel's speech; no separate visible appearance of the Lamb is specified here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Lamb or enact the future events as occurring now.

title: Records hid up and brought forth
summary: The Lamb says he will manifest himself to Nephi's seed, who will write what he ministers to them. After the seed dwindle in unbelief, these things will be hidden and come forth to the Gentiles by the Lamb's gift and power; they will contain his gospel, rock, and salvation.
characters: The angel who appeared to Nephi

explicit_facts.text: The Lamb says he will manifest himself to Nephi's seed, who will write many things he ministers to them.
The Lamb says that after the seed are destroyed and dwindle in unbelief, these things will be hidden and later come forth to the Gentiles by his gift and power.
The Lamb says his gospel, rock, and salvation will be written in them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The records may be represented as the subject of the angel's off-screen teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: The Lamb's appearance, the writings' appearance, and the place or manner of hiding.

spoken_dialogue.text: I will manifest myself unto thy seed,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lamb of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The future events are predictions in speech, not present-tense scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Lamb's manifestation, the destruction of the seed, or the records being hidden or recovered as occurring now.

title: Those who publish peace
summary: The Lamb blesses those who seek to bring forth his Zion, promising them the gift and power of the Holy Ghost and salvation if they endure to the end. The Lamb also speaks of those who publish peace and tidings of great joy.
characters: The angel who appeared to Nephi

explicit_facts.text: The Lamb says those who seek to bring forth his Zion will have the gift and power of the Holy Ghost.
The Lamb says those who endure to the end will be lifted up at the last day and saved in his everlasting kingdom.
The Lamb says those who publish peace and tidings of great joy will be beautiful upon the mountains.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The mountain image may be treated as figurative teaching rather than a literal scene.
unspecified_visual_details: The people meant by those who seek Zion or publish peace, and their appearance or setting.

narration.text: how beautiful upon the mountains shall they be.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage gives blessings and figurative teaching; it does not narrate people on a mountain.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage an unreported gathering or a visible manifestation of the Holy Ghost.

title: Books come to the remnant
summary: The narrator beholds the remnant of the seed of his brethren and the book of the Lamb of God coming from the Gentiles to them. Afterward, he beholds other books coming from the Gentiles to them.
characters: the remnant of the seed of his brethren

explicit_facts.text: The narrator beholds the remnant of the seed of his brethren and the book of the Lamb of God, which comes from the Gentiles to the remnant.
After the book comes to the remnant, the narrator beholds other books coming from the Gentiles to them by the power of the Lamb.
The other books are for convincing the Gentiles, the remnant, and scattered Jews that the records of the prophets and the twelve apostles of the Lamb are true.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The books and the remnant may be shown within the narrator's vision.
unspecified_visual_details: The books' appearance, their carriers, and the remnant's appearance and location are not specified.

narration.text: I beheld the remnant of the seed of my brethren,
I beheld other books, which came forth by the power of the Lamb,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses describe the books coming to the remnant but do not describe a particular delivery scene.
The scattered Jews are mentioned as people to be convinced, not as figures the narrator beholds here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a delivery scene, book titles or markings, or named individuals among the groups.
Do not depict the Lamb's power as a visible event or give the Lamb an invented appearance.

title: The records establish the truth
summary: The angel tells Nephi that the last records will establish the truth of the first, make known what was taken away, and make known the Lamb of God as the Son of the Eternal Father and Savior of the world. The angel says the records will be established as one and foretells a time when the Lamb will manifest himself to all nations.

explicit_facts.text: The angel speaks to Nephi about the last records he has seen among the Gentiles.
The angel says the last records will establish the truth of the first and make known plain and precious things taken away from them.
The angel says the records will make known that the Lamb of God is the Son of the Eternal Father and Savior of the world, and that all must come unto him to be saved.
The angel says the Lamb's words will be made known in the records of Nephi's seed and of the twelve apostles, and that both will be established as one.
The angel foretells that the Lamb will manifest himself to all nations, including Jews and Gentiles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Nephi may be shown listening while the angel speaks.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and the angel's appearance.
The records' physical appearance.
The manner and time of the future manifestation.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel

spoken_dialogue.text: wherefore they both shall be established in one; for there is one God and one Shepherd over all the earth.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel

spoken_dialogue.text: And the time cometh that he shall manifest himself unto all nations,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The angel

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The manifestation is foretold, not narrated as occurring in this scene.
The references to one God and one Shepherd are teachings, not a visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the future manifestation as occurring now.
Do not invent the Lamb's appearance, a specific setting, or additional listeners.
